clinician.trajectory_summary: A 35-year-old male oil palm plantation worker presented with a 2-year history of progressive verrucous plaques on the buttocks, thigh, and scrotum, characterized by painful itchy nodules, ulceration, and foul-smelling seropurulent discharge, forming an annular hyperkeratotic plaque with central healing. He had constitutional symptoms of untreated cough and night sweats without fever for two years. Prior antifungal and antibiotic treatments failed. Punch biopsy revealed marked pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia with epithelioid granulomatous inflammation surrounding caseous necrosis, Langerhans cells, and lymphocytic infiltrates. AFB smear and culture were negative for M. tuberculosis. Chest radiograph revealed extensive pulmonary tuberculosis. The patient was treated with anti-tubercular therapy, showing significant improvement at 2 months and complete resolution with atrophic scarring at 4 months.
